# Local Tiny Agents with AMD NPU and iGPU Acceleration

In this section, we'll show you how to accelerate our end-to-end Tiny Agents application using AMD Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and integrated GPU (iGPU). We then enhance our end-to-end application by providing it with access to local files and creating an assistant to handle sensitive information locally, ensuring maximum privacy.

To enable this, we'll use Lemonade Server, a tool for running models locally with NPU and iGPU acceleration.

## Setup
### Setup Lemonade Server

You can install Lemonade Server on both Windows and Linux. Additional documentation can be found at [lemonade-server.ai](https://lemonade-server.ai/). 

To install Lemonade Server on Windows, simply download and run the latest installer [here](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/releases/latest/download/Lemonade_Server_Installer.exe).

Lemonade Server supports CPU inference across all platforms and engines on Windows x86/x64. GPU acceleration is enabled via the llamacpp engine using Vulkan, with a focus on AMD Ryzen™ AI 7000/8000/300 series and AMD Radeon™ 7000/9000 series. For NPU acceleration, the ONNX Runtime GenAI (OGA) engine enables support for AMD Ryzen™ AI 300 series devices.

Once you have installed Lemonade Server, you can launch it by clicking the `Lemonade` icon added to the Desktop.

To install Lemonade on Linux, first create and activate a venv:

> [!TIP]
> If you don't have `uv` installed, you can install it following the instructions [here](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).

```bash
uv venv --python 3.11
source .venv/bin/activate
```

Then, install the `lemonade-sdk` package:
```bash
uv pip install lemonade-sdk==8.0.3
```

Altenatively, you can also install from source by cloning the repository and building the package:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade-sdk.git
cd lemonade-sdk
pip install -e .
```

Once installed, you can launch Lemonade by running the following command:

```bash
lemonade-server-dev serve
```

Lemonade Server supports CPU inference across all platforms and engines on Windows x86/x64. For GPU acceleration is enabled through llamacpp engine (Vulkan), with a focus on AMD Ryzen™ AI 7000/8000/300 series and Radeon™ 7000/9000 series.

> [!TIP]
> *NPU acceleration is only available for AMD Ryzen™ AI 300 series on Windows.*

### Tiny Agents and NPX Setup

This section of the course assumes you have already installed `npx` and `Tiny Agents`. If you haven't, please refer to the [Tiny Agents](https://huggingface.co/learn/mcp-course/en/unit2/tiny-agents) section of the course. Please make sure to use `huggingface_hub[mcp]==0.33.2`.

## Running your Tiny Agents application with AMD NPU and iGPU

To run your Tiny Agents application with AMD NPU and iGPU, simply point to the MCP server we created in the [previous section](https://huggingface.co/learn/mcp-course/en/unit2/tiny-agents) to the Lemonade Server, as shown below:

```json
{
  "model": "Qwen3-8B-GGUF",
  "endpointUrl": "http://localhost:8000/api/",
  "servers": [
    {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\npx.cmd",
      "args": [
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://localhost:7860/gradio_api/mcp/sse"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "model": "Qwen3-8B-GGUF",
  "endpointUrl": "http://localhost:8000/api/",
  "servers": [
    {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://localhost:7860/gradio_api/mcp/sse"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

You can then choose from a variety of models to run on your local machine. For this example, used the [`Qwen3-8B-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B-GGUF) model, which runs efficiently on AMD GPUs through Vulkan acceleration. You can find the list of models supported and even import your own models by navigating to http://localhost:8000/#model-management.

## Creating an assistant to handle sensitive information locally

![Lemonade Server Interface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lemonade-sdk/assets/refs/heads/main/huggingface_course/hf_lemonade.png)

Now let's enhance our end-to-end application by enabling access to local files and introducing an assistant that processes sensitive information entirely on-device. Specifically, this assistant will help us evaluate candidate resumes and support decision-making in the hiring process—all while keeping the data private and secure.

To do this, we'll use the [Desktop Commander](https://github.com/wonderwhy-er/DesktopCommanderMCP) MCP server, which allows you to run commands on your local machine and provides comprehensive file system access, terminal control, and code editing capabilities.

Let's setup a project with a basic Tiny Agent.

```bash
mkdir file-assistant
cd file-assistant
```

Let's then create a new `agent.json` file in the `file-assistant` folder.

```json
{
  "model": "user.jan-nano",
  "endpointUrl": "http://localhost:8000/api/",
  "servers": [
    {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\npx.cmd",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "model": "user.jan-nano",
  "endpointUrl": "http://localhost:8000/api/",
  "servers": [
    {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Finally, we have to download the `Jan Nano` model. You can do this by navigating to http://localhost:8000/#model-management, clicking on `Add a Model` and providing the following information:

```
Model Name: user.jan-nano
Checkpoint: Menlo/Jan-nano-gguf:jan-nano-4b-Q4_0.gguf
Recipe: llamacpp
```

![Custom Model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lemonade-sdk/assets/refs/heads/main/huggingface_course/custom_model.png)

All done! Now let's give it a try.

### Taking it for a spin

![recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lemonade-sdk/assets/refs/heads/main/huggingface_course/recording.gif)

Our goal is to create an assistant that can help us handle sensitive information locally. To do this, we'll first create a job description file for our assistant to work with.

Create a file called `job_description.md` in the `file-assistant` folder.

```md
# Senior Food Technology Engineer

## About the Role
We're seeking a culinary innovator to transform cooking processes into precise algorithms and AI systems.

## What You'll Do
- Convert cooking instructions into measurable algorithms
- Develop AI-powered kitchen tools
- Create food quality assessment systems
- Build recipe-following AI models

## Requirements
- MS in Computer Science (food-related thesis preferred)
- Python and PyTorch expertise
- Proven experience combining food science with ML
- Strong communication skills using culinary metaphors

## Perks
- Access to experimental kitchen
- Continuous taste-testing opportunities
- Collaborative tech-foodie team environment

*Note: Must attend conferences and publish on algorithmic cooking optimization.*

```

Now, let's create a `candidates` folder inside the `file-assistant` folder and add a sample resume file for our assistant to work with.

```bash
mkdir candidates
touch candidates/john_resume.md
```

```md

- Designed efficient mapo tofu quality estimation method using thermometer

## Education

## Skills

**Programming Languages:** Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML/CSS, Java
```

```
Tool REDACTED

(...)

The job description for the Senior Food Technology Engineer position emphasizes the need for a candidate who can bridge the gap between food science and artificial intelligence (...). Candidates are also expected to attend conferences and publish research on algorithmic cooking optimization.
```

### Exploring other models and acceleration options

In the example above, the Jan-Nano model leveraged Vulkan acceleration for efficient local LLM inference on AMD GPUs. Models such as `Llama-xLAM-2-8b-fc-r-Hybrid` are specifically fine-tuned for tool-calling and deliver fast, responsive performance!

**No one has built a Lemonade MCP server.** AMD's approach is the inverse — Lemonade is the *inference backend* that MCP agents call via OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Our MCP server flips this: it exposes Lemonade's unique capabilities (model management, multi-backend routing, image gen, TTS, transcription, reranking) as MCP **tools** that Claude Code can invoke directly. This is novel.

**Key finding from the HF tutorial:** `Qwen3-8B-GGUF` is the recommended model for tool-calling with Vulkan acceleration. And `Llama-xLAM-2-8b-fc-r-Hybrid` is specifically fine-tuned for tool-calling on NPU+iGPU hybrid. Both are worth pulling.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

"""Lemonade MCP server — local inference tools for Claude Code.

Exposes Lemonade server capabilities as MCP tools: chat, embeddings,
image generation, TTS, transcription, model management, and health.

IMPORTANT (L274): No network calls at import time. Lazy init only.
IMPORTANT (L275): No stdout output during init (stdio transport).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

mcp = FastMCP(
    "lemonade",
    description="Local AI inference via Lemonade server (AMD Strix Halo)",
)

# Lazy client — no network at import
_client = None


def _get_client():
    """Lazy-init the Lemonade HTTP client."""
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        from .client import LemonadeClient
        _client = LemonadeClient()
    return _client


# ── Health & Status ─────────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_health() -> str:
    """Check Lemonade server health, loaded models, and performance stats."""
    c = _get_client()
    health = c.health()
    stats = c.stats()

    loaded = health.get("all_models_loaded", [])
    model_lines = []
    for m in loaded:
        model_lines.append(
            f"  {m['model_name']} (type={m.get('type')}, device={m.get('device')}, recipe={m.get('recipe')})"
        )

    return (
        f"Status: {health.get('status')}\n"
        f"Version: {health.get('version')}\n"
        f"Loaded models ({len(loaded)}):\n" + "\n".join(model_lines or ["  (none)"]) + "\n"
        f"TPS: {stats.get('tokens_per_second', 'N/A')}\n"
        f"TTFT: {stats.get('time_to_first_token', 'N/A')}ms\n"
        f"Max models: {json.dumps(health.get('max_models', {}))}"
    )


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_system_info() -> str:
    """Show hardware capabilities and installed backends."""
    c = _get_client()
    info = c.system_info()
    devices = info.get("devices", {})
    recipes = info.get("recipes", {})

    lines = ["## Devices"]
    for name in ["cpu", "amd_igpu", "amd_npu"]:
        dev = devices.get(name)
        if dev and dev.get("available"):
            lines.append(f"  {name}: {dev.get('name', '?')} ({dev.get('family', '?')})")

    lines.append("\n## Backends")
    for rname, rdata in sorted(recipes.items()):
        for bname, binfo in rdata.get("backends", {}).items():
            state = binfo.get("state", "?")
            icon = "✓" if state == "installed" else "○" if state == "installable" else "✗"
            lines.append(f"  [{icon}] {rname}/{bname}: {state}")

    return "\n".join(lines)


# ── Model Management ───────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_list_models(show_all: bool = False) -> str:
    """List available Lemonade models. Set show_all=true to include undownloaded."""
    c = _get_client()
    models = c.list_models(show_all=show_all)

    lines = [f"{'Downloaded' if not show_all else 'All'} models ({len(models)}):"]
    for m in models:
        dl = "✓" if m.get("downloaded") else " "
        size = m.get("size", 0)
        size_gb = f"{size / (1024**3):.1f}GB" if size > 0 else "remote"
        labels = m.get("labels", [])
        recipe = m.get("recipe", "?")
        lines.append(f"  [{dl}] {m['id']:40} {size_gb:>8}  recipe={recipe}  {labels}")

    return "\n".join(lines)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_pull_model(model_name: str) -> str:
    """Download a model by name. Use lemonade_list_models(show_all=true) to see available names."""
    c = _get_client()
    result = c.pull_model(model_name)
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_load_model(
    model_name: str,
    ctx_size: int = 8192,
    backend: str = "vulkan",
) -> str:
    """Load a model into memory. Backend: vulkan (GPU), cpu, npu. Watch OOM on large models."""
    c = _get_client()
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"ctx_size": ctx_size}
    # Only set llamacpp_backend for llamacpp recipe models (GGUF)
    if "GGUF" in model_name or "gguf" in model_name.lower():
        kwargs["llamacpp_backend"] = backend
    result = c.load_model(model_name, **kwargs)
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_unload_model(model_name: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Unload a model from memory (frees RAM/VRAM). None = unload all."""
    c = _get_client()
    result = c.unload_model(model_name)
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_install_backend(recipe: str, backend: str) -> str:
    """Install a Lemonade backend. Recipes: llamacpp, kokoro, whispercpp, sd-cpp. Backends: vulkan, cpu."""
    c = _get_client()
    result = c.install_backend(recipe, backend)
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2)


# ── Inference ──────────────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_chat(
    prompt: str,
    model: str = "",
    system: str = "",
    temperature: float = 0.7,
    max_tokens: int = 512,
) -> str:
    """Chat with a loaded LLM. Leave model empty to use whatever is loaded."""
    c = _get_client()
    if not model:
        health = c.health()
        loaded = [m for m in health.get("all_models_loaded", []) if m.get("type") == "llm"]
        if not loaded:
            return "Error: No LLM loaded. Use lemonade_load_model first."
        model = loaded[0]["model_name"]

    messages = []
    if system:
        messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})

    result = c.chat(model, messages, temperature=temperature, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    content = result.get("choices", [{}])[0].get("message", {}).get("content", "")

    # Filter NPU pad tokens
    content = content.replace("<pad>", "").replace("<eos>", "").strip()
    if not content:
        return f"Model '{model}' returned empty response (may need a chat-capable model)."
    return content


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_embed(texts: list[str], model: str = "embed-gemma-300m-FLM") -> str:
    """Get vector embeddings for texts. Returns dimensions and first 5 values per vector."""
    c = _get_client()
    vectors = c.embed(model, texts)

    lines = [f"Embedded {len(vectors)} texts (dim={len(vectors[0]) if vectors else 0}):"]
    for i, vec in enumerate(vectors):
        preview = ", ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in vec[:5])
        lines.append(f"  [{i}] [{preview}, ...] (norm={sum(v*v for v in vec)**0.5:.4f})")
    return "\n".join(lines)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_rerank(query: str, documents: list[str], model: str = "") -> str:
    """Rerank documents by relevance to a query. Returns sorted results."""
    c = _get_client()
    if not model:
        model = "jina-reranker-v2-GGUF"
    results = c.rerank(model, query, documents)
    sorted_results = sorted(results, key=lambda r: r.get("relevance_score", 0), reverse=True)
    lines = [f"Query: {query[:80]}"]
    for r in sorted_results:
        idx = r.get("index", "?")
        score = r.get("relevance_score", 0)
        doc_preview = documents[idx][:60] if isinstance(idx, int) and idx < len(documents) else "?"
        lines.append(f"  [{score:.4f}] doc[{idx}]: {doc_preview}...")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ── Image Generation ───────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_generate_image(
    prompt: str,
    output_path: str = "generated_image.png",
    model: str = "Flux-2-Klein-4B",
    size: str = "512x512",
    steps: int = 20,
    cfg_scale: float = 7.0,
) -> str:
    """Generate an image from a text prompt. Saves PNG to output_path."""
    c = _get_client()
    b64 = c.generate_image(model, prompt, size=size, steps=steps, cfg_scale=cfg_scale)
    out = Path(output_path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(b64))
    return f"Image saved to {out.resolve()} ({out.stat().st_size / 1024:.0f}KB)"


# ── Audio ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_speak(
    text: str,
    output_path: str = "speech.wav",
    voice: str = "af_heart",
    model: str = "kokoro-v1",
) -> str:
    """Convert text to speech. Saves audio to output_path."""
    c = _get_client()
    audio = c.speak(text, model=model, voice=voice)
    out = Path(output_path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_bytes(audio)
    return f"Audio saved to {out.resolve()} ({out.stat().st_size / 1024:.0f}KB, {len(text)} chars)"


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_transcribe(audio_path: str, model: str = "Whisper-Large-v3-Turbo") -> str:
    """Transcribe audio file to text. Accepts WAV format."""
    c = _get_client()
    text = c.transcribe(audio_path, model=model)
    return text if text else "No transcription produced."


# ── Entry Point ────────────────────────────────────────────────


def main():
    """Run the MCP server (stdio transport)."""
    mcp.run(transport="stdio")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

toolUseResult.originalFile:
"""Lemonade MCP server — local inference tools for Claude Code.

Exposes Lemonade server capabilities as MCP tools: chat, embeddings,
image generation, TTS, transcription, model management, and health.

IMPORTANT (L274): No network calls at import time. Lazy init only.
IMPORTANT (L275): No stdout output during init (stdio transport).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

mcp = FastMCP(
    "lemonade",
    description="Local AI inference via Lemonade server (AMD Strix Halo)",
)

# Lazy client — no network at import
_client = None


def _get_client():
    """Lazy-init the Lemonade HTTP client."""
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        from .client import LemonadeClient
        _client = LemonadeClient()
    return _client


# ── Health & Status ─────────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_health() -> str:
    """Check Lemonade server health, loaded models, and performance stats."""
    c = _get_client()
    health = c.health()
    stats = c.stats()

    loaded = health.get("all_models_loaded", [])
    model_lines = []
    for m in loaded:
        model_lines.append(
            f"  {m['model_name']} (type={m.get('type')}, device={m.get('device')}, recipe={m.get('recipe')})"
        )

    return (
        f"Status: {health.get('status')}\n"
        f"Version: {health.get('version')}\n"
        f"Loaded models ({len(loaded)}):\n" + "\n".join(model_lines or ["  (none)"]) + "\n"
        f"TPS: {stats.get('tokens_per_second', 'N/A')}\n"
        f"TTFT: {stats.get('time_to_first_token', 'N/A')}ms\n"
        f"Max models: {json.dumps(health.get('max_models', {}))}"
    )


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_system_info() -> str:
    """Show hardware capabilities and installed backends."""
    c = _get_client()
    info = c.system_info()
    devices = info.get("devices", {})
    recipes = info.get("recipes", {})

    lines = ["## Devices"]
    for name in ["cpu", "amd_igpu", "amd_npu"]:
        dev = devices.get(name)
        if dev and dev.get("available"):
            lines.append(f"  {name}: {dev.get('name', '?')} ({dev.get('family', '?')})")

    lines.append("\n## Backends")
    for rname, rdata in sorted(recipes.items()):
        for bname, binfo in rdata.get("backends", {}).items():
            state = binfo.get("state", "?")
            icon = "✓" if state == "installed" else "○" if state == "installable" else "✗"
            lines.append(f"  [{icon}] {rname}/{bname}: {state}")

    return "\n".join(lines)


# ── Model Management ───────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_list_models(show_all: bool = False) -> str:
    """List available Lemonade models. Set show_all=true to include undownloaded."""
    c = _get_client()
    models = c.list_models(show_all=show_all)

    lines = [f"{'Downloaded' if not show_all else 'All'} models ({len(models)}):"]
    for m in models:
        dl = "✓" if m.get("downloaded") else " "
        size = m.get("size", 0)
        size_gb = f"{size / (1024**3):.1f}GB" if size > 0 else "remote"
        labels = m.get("labels", [])
        recipe = m.get("recipe", "?")
        lines.append(f"  [{dl}] {m['id']:40} {size_gb:>8}  recipe={recipe}  {labels}")

    return "\n".join(lines)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_pull_model(model_name: str) -> str:
    """Download a model by name. Use lemonade_list_models(show_all=true) to see available names."""
    c = _get_client()
    result = c.pull_model(model_name)
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_load_model(
    model_name: str,
    ctx_size: int = 8192,
    backend: str = "vulkan",
) -> str:
    """Load a model into memory. Backend: vulkan (GPU), cpu, npu. Watch OOM on large models."""
    c = _get_client()
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"ctx_size": ctx_size}
    # Only set llamacpp_backend for llamacpp recipe models (GGUF)
    if "GGUF" in model_name or "gguf" in model_name.lower():
        kwargs["llamacpp_backend"] = backend
    result = c.load_model(model_name, **kwargs)
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_unload_model(model_name: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Unload a model from memory (frees RAM/VRAM). None = unload all."""
    c = _get_client()
    result = c.unload_model(model_name)
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_install_backend(recipe: str, backend: str) -> str:
    """Install a Lemonade backend. Recipes: llamacpp, kokoro, whispercpp, sd-cpp. Backends: vulkan, cpu."""
    c = _get_client()
    result = c.install_backend(recipe, backend)
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2)


# ── Inference ──────────────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_chat(
    prompt: str,
    model: str = "",
    system: str = "",
    temperature: float = 0.7,
    max_tokens: int = 512,
) -> str:
    """Chat with a loaded LLM. Leave model empty to use whatever is loaded."""
    c = _get_client()
    if not model:
        health = c.health()
        loaded = [m for m in health.get("all_models_loaded", []) if m.get("type") == "llm"]
        if not loaded:
            return "Error: No LLM loaded. Use lemonade_load_model first."
        model = loaded[0]["model_name"]

    messages = []
    if system:
        messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})

    result = c.chat(model, messages, temperature=temperature, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    content = result.get("choices", [{}])[0].get("message", {}).get("content", "")

    # Filter NPU pad tokens
    content = content.replace("<pad>", "").replace("<eos>", "").strip()
    if not content:
        return f"Model '{model}' returned empty response (may need a chat-capable model)."
    return content


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_embed(texts: list[str], model: str = "embed-gemma-300m-FLM") -> str:
    """Get vector embeddings for texts. Returns dimensions and first 5 values per vector."""
    c = _get_client()
    vectors = c.embed(model, texts)

    lines = [f"Embedded {len(vectors)} texts (dim={len(vectors[0]) if vectors else 0}):"]
    for i, vec in enumerate(vectors):
        preview = ", ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in vec[:5])
        lines.append(f"  [{i}] [{preview}, ...] (norm={sum(v*v for v in vec)**0.5:.4f})")
    return "\n".join(lines)


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_rerank(query: str, documents: list[str], model: str = "") -> str:
    """Rerank documents by relevance to a query. Returns sorted results."""
    c = _get_client()
    if not model:
        model = "jina-reranker-v2-GGUF"
    results = c.rerank(model, query, documents)
    sorted_results = sorted(results, key=lambda r: r.get("relevance_score", 0), reverse=True)
    lines = [f"Query: {query[:80]}"]
    for r in sorted_results:
        idx = r.get("index", "?")
        score = r.get("relevance_score", 0)
        doc_preview = documents[idx][:60] if isinstance(idx, int) and idx < len(documents) else "?"
        lines.append(f"  [{score:.4f}] doc[{idx}]: {doc_preview}...")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ── Image Generation ───────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_generate_image(
    prompt: str,
    output_path: str = "generated_image.png",
    model: str = "Flux-2-Klein-4B",
    size: str = "512x512",
    steps: int = 20,
    cfg_scale: float = 7.0,
) -> str:
    """Generate an image from a text prompt. Saves PNG to output_path."""
    c = _get_client()
    b64 = c.generate_image(model, prompt, size=size, steps=steps, cfg_scale=cfg_scale)
    out = Path(output_path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(b64))
    return f"Image saved to {out.resolve()} ({out.stat().st_size / 1024:.0f}KB)"


# ── Audio ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_speak(
    text: str,
    output_path: str = "speech.wav",
    voice: str = "af_heart",
    model: str = "kokoro-v1",
) -> str:
    """Convert text to speech. Saves audio to output_path."""
    c = _get_client()
    audio = c.speak(text, model=model, voice=voice)
    out = Path(output_path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_bytes(audio)
    return f"Audio saved to {out.resolve()} ({out.stat().st_size / 1024:.0f}KB, {len(text)} chars)"


@mcp.tool()
def lemonade_transcribe(audio_path: str, model: str = "Whisper-Large-v3-Turbo") -> str:
    """Transcribe audio file to text. Accepts WAV format."""
    c = _get_client()
    text = c.transcribe(audio_path, model=model)
    return text if text else "No transcription produced."


# ── Entry Point ────────────────────────────────────────────────


def main():
    """Run the MCP server (stdio transport)."""
    mcp.run(transport="stdio")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**The Lemonade Developer Challenge is a perfect fit for this work.** They're giving away AMD Strix Halo laptops (the exact hardware we're running on) for projects that integrate Lemonade into apps/workflows. What we've built today — CAS dogfooding through Lemonade + an MCP server that exposes all Lemonade capabilities + FLUME journey visualization via Stable Diffusion — hits all their criteria: community impact (open-source MCP server anyone can use), technical depth (CAS cognitive architecture + compound engineering loop), and creativity (rendering 12D manifold trajectories as images via local inference).
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Here's what we've built and where it connects to the Lemonade Developer Challenge:

## Deliverables This Session

### 1. CAS Classifier Adapter (Dogfooding)
- **`src/cohezion/compound/cas_classifier.py`** — Thin sync adapter mapping CAS's 10 cognitive faculties → ContextPolicy task classification via Lemonade
- **Wired into CompoundExecutor** — auto-detects Lemonade, falls back to keywords
- **Training data flywheel** — every classification becomes fine-tuning data
- **21 tests passing**

### 2. Lemonade MCP Server (`lemonade-mcp/`)
13 tools exposing the full Lemonade API to Claude Code and any MCP client:

| Tool | What It Does |
|------|-------------|
| `lemonade_health` | Server status, loaded models, TPS |
| `lemonade_system_info` | Hardware + installed backends |
| `lemonade_list_models` | Browse 115+ available models |
| `lemonade_pull_model` | Download models |
| `lemonade_load_model` | Load with backend selection (vulkan/cpu/npu) |
| `lemonade_unload_model` | Free memory |
| `lemonade_install_backend` | Install llamacpp-vulkan, kokoro, whispercpp, sd-cpp |
| `lemonade_chat` | Chat completion |
| `lemonade_embed` | Vector embeddings |
| `lemonade_rerank` | Document relevance scoring |
| `lemonade_generate_image` | Stable Diffusion / Flux image gen |
| `lemonade_speak` | Text-to-speech (Kokoro) |
| `lemonade_transcribe` | Speech-to-text (Whisper) |

### 3. PRIME Skill
- **`LEMONADE_LOCAL_INFERENCE_PRIME.md`** — Complete reference for model stack, OOM prevention, API usage, backend installation, all using Vulkan for GPU

## For the Challenge Submission

What we've built is exactly what they're looking for — "Integrate Lemonade into an app/workflow and demo it":

1. **Cohezion's Compound Engineering Loop** uses Lemonade for task classification (CAS), creating a cognitive architecture where specialized models handle perception, reasoning, and metacognition
2. **The MCP server** is an open-source tool that makes Lemonade accessible to the entire Claude Code / MCP ecosystem — not just Cohezion
3. **FLUME journey rendering** via Stable Diffusion on the iGPU means agent trajectories through the 12D manifold become visual art, generated locally

**Next steps to unlock the full stack:**
- Install `llamacpp-vulkan` backend (for chat-capable GGUF models)
- Pull `Qwen3-8B-GGUF` (recommended for tool-calling)
- Install `sd-cpp-vulkan` backend + pull `Flux-2-Klein-4B` (for FLUME renders)
- Install `kokoro-cpu` + pull `kokoro-v1` (for narration)
- Register the MCP server in `~/.claude/settings.json`

Want me to install the backends and pull the models now? That would activate the full pipeline for the challenge demo.

- [Hugging Face MCP Course: Lemonade Server](https://huggingface.co/learn/mcp-course/en/unit2/lemonade-server)

# Swarm Orchestration Rules

- KISS principle: if simple one-pass logic works, do not use a multi-agent swarm
- All swarm operations must be observable — expose states and confidence levels before taking action
- Use idempotency keys for significant actions (Deterministic Responsibility)
- Route complex problems through Expert Domain Lattice: Architect, Engineer, Biologist, Quantum HW, Quantum Algo
- `smart_router.py` and `model_manager.py` are the central routing/model lifecycle modules
- Respect global Ollama concurrency limit of 4 — `dynamic_model_router.py` must enforce this
- Prefer local Ollama models over cloud API calls to stay within cost guardrails
- Democratic debates (`democratic_debate.py`, `glass_box_debate.py`) must log all agent votes and reasoning for transparency

# Swarm Orchestration Rules

- KISS principle: if simple one-pass logic works, do not use a multi-agent swarm
- All swarm operations must be observable — expose states and confidence levels before taking action
- Use idempotency keys for significant actions (Deterministic Responsibility)
- Route complex problems through Expert Domain Lattice: Architect, Engineer, Biologist, Quantum HW, Quantum Algo
- `smart_router.py` and `model_manager.py` are the central routing/model lifecycle modules
- Respect global Ollama concurrency limit of 4 — `dynamic_model_router.py` must enforce this
- Prefer local Ollama models over cloud API calls to stay within cost guardrails
- Democratic debates (`democratic_debate.py`, `glass_box_debate.py`) must log all agent votes and reasoning for transparency

Now I have the complete picture. Here's the multimodal pipeline:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**The infrastructure is 80% there but disconnected.** JourneyTracker produces 12D trajectory points. JourneyNarrator is a stub (original removed). The API has `/journeys/{id}/visualize` and `/journeys/{id}/plot` endpoints but they raise "unavailable." The FLUME VAE encodes to 256D. All the data flows exist — what's missing is the rendering layer connecting trajectory data to Lemonade's image/audio/text generation. This is the wiring, not new modules.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Here's the full multimodal picture of what Lemonade can do for FLUME agentic journeys:

## The Four Modalities

### Text (LLM)
**Available now**: 41 LLM models + 29 vision models + 17 tool-calling models

| What | Model | Backend | Status |
|------|-------|---------|--------|
| Task classification (CAS) | `gemma3-4b-FLM` | flm/NPU | Loaded (pad token issue) |
| Chat/reasoning | `Qwen3-8B-GGUF` | llamacpp/vulkan | Need to install + pull |
| Tool-calling agent | `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF` | llamacpp/vulkan | Need to install + pull |
| Journey narration | Any chat model | llamacpp/vulkan | JourneyNarrator is a stub — needs rewiring |

**For journeys**: `JourneyNarrator.generate_narration()` is currently a no-op stub. Wire it to `lemonade_chat` with a prompt like: *"Narrate this agent's journey through 12D manifold space. Coherence went from 0.3 to 0.5 over 8 steps. The agent started in EXPLORATORY mode and converged to HIHO stability."*

### Images (Stable Diffusion / Flux)
**Available**: 11 image models including Flux-2-Klein (4B and 9B), SDXL, and RealESRGAN upscaler

| What | Model | Backend | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|---------|
| Journey keyframes | `Flux-2-Klein-4B` | sd-cpp/vulkan | Render 12D trajectory as abstract art |
| Style variations | `SD-Turbo` | sd-cpp/vulkan | Fast drafts (1-4 steps) |
| Upscaling | `RealESRGAN-x4plus` | sd-cpp/cpu | 4x resolution for final renders |
| Image editing | `Flux-2-Klein-4B` | sd-cpp/vulkan | Inpainting with masks |

**For journeys**: Each `TrajectoryPoint` has 12 dimensions + coherence. Map these to prompt elements:
- Coherence 0.0-0.3 → "chaotic, fragmented, dark red nebula"
- Coherence 0.3-0.5 → "converging, crystallizing, blue-gold lattice"  
- Coherence 0.5 → "perfect HIHO balance, radiant symmetry, emerald equilibrium"
- Coherence 0.5-1.0 → "over-structured, rigid, ice-white crystal"

Generate a keyframe per trajectory point → stitch into an animation with ffmpeg.

### Audio (TTS + Transcription)
**Available**: Kokoro TTS (1 model) + Whisper ASR (7 models)

| What | Model | Backend | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|---------|
| Journey narration | `kokoro-v1` | kokoro/cpu | Speak the journey story |
| Voice input | `Whisper-Large-v3-Turbo` | whispercpp/cpu | Voice commands to agents |
| Fast transcription | `whisper-v3-turbo-FLM` | flm/NPU | Real-time on NPU |

**For journeys**: Kokoro has multiple voices (`af_heart`, `af_bella`, etc.). Assign voices to archetypes: Explorer gets an excited voice, Stabilizer gets calm, Drifter gets uncertain.

### Video (Composite Pipeline)
**Not a single model — it's a pipeline:**

```
JourneyTracker (12D points)
  → LLM generates per-frame prompts (text)
  → Flux/SD renders keyframes (images)
  → RealESRGAN upscales to 4K (images)
  → Kokoro narrates the journey (audio)
  → ffmpeg stitches frames + audio → MP4 (video)
```

Perfect. Now I have all the information I need. Let me provide a comprehensive report:

## Comprehensive Analysis of Cohezion's Dynamic Modularity & Routing Infrastructure

Based on thorough exploration of the codebase, here's what exists and what gaps are critical for Lemonade integration:

### 1. **DynamicModelRouter** (`src/cohezion/swarm/dynamic_model_router.py`)

**Class Structure:**
- `DynamicModelRouter` - Core routing engine
- `MemoryBandwidthAnalyzer` - Real-time RAM/L3/DDR5 analysis
- `AdaptiveTemplateManager` - Template format conversion (chatml, microsoft, llama3)
- `ModelConfig` (dataclass) - Quantization-aware model metadata
- `ModelTier` (Enum) - MICRO/SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE/ULTRA with concurrent limits

**Key Methods:**
- `select_optimal_model(request)` - Selects model based on IDE priority + task type + memory pressure
- `calculate_model_score()` - Compound scoring (15+ factors: memory fit, TPS, cache hit rate, context window)
- `execute_request()` - Routes through Ollama HTTP API (`/api/generate`)
- `ollama_generate()` - HTTP POST to local Ollama server
- `record_performance()` - Tracks execution metrics to performance_history

**Tracked State:**
- `active_models: dict[str, ModelConfig]` - Currently loaded models
- `performance_history: list[dict]` - 1,000-entry rolling window
- `request_queue: asyncio.Queue` - Async request queueing
- Model registry: 13 models (5 ultra-large, 2 cloud: Gemini 3.0 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet)

**CRITICAL FINDING:** Router calls ONLY Ollama HTTP API. Cloud models (Gemini, Claude) are in the registry but NOT actually called—they're stubs for fallback chaining only.

---

### 2. **CostAwareRouter** (`src/cohezion/swarm/cost_aware_router.py`)

**Class Structure:**
- `CostAwareRouter` - Smart cost optimization router
- `QueryComplexityAnalyzer` - Detects complexity tier (SIMPLE/MEDIUM/COMPLEX)
- `ModelRoutingDecision` (dataclass) - Includes OI-MAS confidence (0.0-1.0)
- `RoutingStatistics` (dataclass) - Aggregated metrics

**Key Methods:**
- `select_model(query, max_cost_usd, cache_hit_rate)` - Returns (decision, can_proceed)
- `_optimize_model_selection()` - Cost/token ratio optimization with aggressive routing
- `_check_context_window()` - Escalation to larger-context models (phi3 → qwen3 → deepseek → gemini)
- `_apply_r_zero_adjustment()` - Escalates when local model success rate < 80%
- `record_execution()` - Tracks costs, success, and updates thresholds dynamically
- `apply_degradation_feedback()` - Callback from DegradationDetector (CRITICAL alerts force upgrade)
- `_compute_routing_confidence()` - OI-MAS joint role+scale scoring

**Model Tiers:**
- **SIMPLE** (70%): phi3:mini → qwen3-coder:32b → deepseek-r1:8b
- **MEDIUM** (20%): qwen3-coder:32b → deepseek-r1:8b → gemini-2.5-flash
- **COMPLEX** (10%): deepseek-r1:8b → gemini-2.5-pro

**Cost Model:**
- Local models: $0.00 (9 models)
- Gemini tiers: $0.075/M (lite) → $0.30/M (flash) → $2.00/M (pro)
- Context escalation chain: 4K → 32K → 64K → 128K → 1M (cloud)

**Integration Points:**
- `BudgetEnforcer.check_budget()` - Hard stop if budget exceeded
- `SessionCostTracker.track_usage_fast()` - Cost tracking
- `ModelPoolManager` (optional) - Checks model availability
- `LocalModelOptimizer` (R-Zero) - Lazy-loaded for success-rate feedback
- **Pool manager is OPTIONAL and when absent, proceeds best-effort**

**CRITICAL FINDING:** CostAwareRouter DOES NOT call any actual models. It selects model names and returns decisions. Actual execution is caller's responsibility. No Lemonade integration exists.

---

### 3. **SmartRouter** (`src/cohezion/swarm/smart_router.py`)

**Class Structure:**
- `SmartRouter` - Task classification + capability matching router
- `ModelProfile` (dataclass) - Name, capabilities, context, speed_tier (1-5), quality_tier (1-5)
- `RoutingDecision` (dataclass) - Task type, selected model, fallbacks, confidence
- `AgentAction` (dataclass) - Execution log for knowledge base persistence
- `TaskType` (Enum) - ANALYSIS, SYNTHESIS, CREATIVE, CODING, FACTUAL, DEBATE, SUMMARY
- `ModelCapability` (Enum) - FAST, ACCURATE, CREATIVE, LARGE_CONTEXT, CODING

**Key Methods:**
- `classify_task(prompt)` - Keyword-based task classification
- `route(task_type)` - Capability matching + strategy scoring (efficiency/quality/speed)
- `execute()` - Calls Ollama `/api/generate` with fallback chain
- `refresh_models()` - Queries Ollama `/api/tags`
- `save_action_log()` - Persists execution logs to `knowledge_graph/universe_nodes/actions/`

**Strategy Modes:**
- **Efficiency** (default): balance speed + quality
- **Quality**: prioritize best results
- **Speed**: prioritize fastest response

**Model Registry:** 18 local models (qwen, phi, deepseek, gemma, gpt-oss, minicpm-v)

**CRITICAL FINDING:** SmartRouter is the MOST FUNCTIONAL but STILL OLLAMA-ONLY. It logs actions to knowledge graph (good pattern) but does NOT call external APIs.

---

### 4. **ModelPoolManager** (`src/cohezion/swarm/model_pool_manager.py`)

**Class Structure:**
- `ModelPoolManager` - 3-tier hot/warm/cold model lifecycle
- `PooledModel` (from model_pool_config) - Name, tier, size_gb, loaded, healthy, last_used
- `TierConfig` - Max concurrent, memory thresholds, eviction timeouts
- `PoolStatus` - Snapshot of pool state

**Key Methods:**
- `initialize()` - Queries Ollama `/api/tags` and `/api/ps`
- `ensure_loaded(model_name)` - Load with eviction if at capacity
- `health_check()` - Pings model with trivial prompt
- `demote_under_pressure()` - Evicts COLD/WARM models when memory pressure > threshold
- `promote()` - Escalates model tier (cold → warm → hot)

**Integration:**
- Uses `MemoryBandwidthAnalyzer` from DynamicModelRouter
- Communicates via Ollama HTTP `/api/generate` with `keep_alive` control
- Works with CostAwareRouter to check availability (optional)

**CRITICAL FINDING:** This manager is PURELY FOR OLLAMA LOCAL MODELS. No cloud provider lifecycle management exists.

---

### 5. **Model Providers** (`src/cohezion/swarm/providers/`)

**Abstract Base:**
```python
class ModelProvider(ABC):
    async def generate(model: str, prompt: str, ...) -> GenerationResult
    async def list_models() -> list[str]
    async def health_check() -> dict[str, Any]
```

**Implementations:**
1. **OllamaProvider** - Local Ollama HTTP client
2. **GeminiProvider** - Google Gemini Cloud API (FULLY IMPLEMENTED)
   - Multi-tier: Flash-Lite ($0.075/M), Flash ($0.30/M), Pro ($2.00/M)
   - Context: 1M-2M
   - Status: WORKING (calls actual Gemini API)
3. **Gemma4Provider** - Extends OllamaProvider (Gemma4-specific tuning)
4. **RegistryPattern** - `register_model_provider(name, class)` enables runtime swapping

**CRITICAL FINDING:** Provider pattern exists and is extensible, but NO LemonadeProvider exists. This is the integration point.

---

### 6. **Model Adapter** (`src/cohezion/swarm/model_adapter.py`)

```python
class SmartRouterAdapter:
    """Translates SmartRouter interface → TokenEfficientClient interface"""
    async def select_optimal_model(context: dict) -> ModelSelection
```

Maps free-form task strings to SmartRouter TaskType enums. Minimal translation layer—proves the pattern works.

---

### 7. **No Dynamic Modularity Skill Found**

I searched thoroughly:
- No `cohezion-dynamic-modularity` PRIME skill file exists
- No hotswapping or runtime module loading infrastructure found
- The term "dynamic modularity" appears ONLY in comments (this document header and discussions)
- The **DynamicModelRouter is static model loading from a registry, NOT hot-swappable modules**

---

## **Integration Gaps for Lemonade**

| Component | Current State | Gap for Lemonade |
|-----------|---------------|------------------|
| **DynamicModelRouter** | Ollama-only, local models hardcoded | No Lemonade provider endpoint, no async client |
| **CostAwareRouter** | Selects models, doesn't execute | Needs to be wired to actual Lemonade calls |
| **SmartRouter** | Ollama-only with action logging | Same gap as Dynamic |
| **ModelPoolManager** | Ollama lifecycle (load/unload) | Lemonade has different lifecycle API (`/api/v1/load`, `/api/v1/unload`) |
| **Provider Pattern** | GeminiProvider works, pattern proven | **MUST BUILD:** LemonadeProvider(ModelProvider) |
| **Health Checks** | Per-model HTTP ping | Lemonade health is at `/api/v1/health` (global) |
| **Cost Tracking** | Per-model metrics | Lemonade exposes `/api/v1/stats` (need mapping) |
| **Hotswapping** | DOES NOT EXIST | Not in scope of current architecture |

---

## **Which Routers Call Actual APIs?**

**ONLY CALL ACTUAL INFERENCE:**
1. **GeminiProvider.generate()** - YES, calls Google Gemini API ✓
2. **OllamaProvider.generate()** - YES, calls local Ollama HTTP ✓
3. **DynamicModelRouter.ollama_generate()** - YES, calls Ollama HTTP ✓
4. **SmartRouter.execute()** - YES, calls Ollama HTTP ✓
5. **CostAwareRouter.select_model()** - NO, returns decision only
6. **SmartRouterAdapter** - NO, just translates interfaces
7. **GeminiProvider, DynamicModelRouter stubs** - Cloud models in config but never called (fallbacks only)

---

## **Recommended Wiring for Lemonade**

### Phase 1: Create LemonadeProvider
```python
class LemonadeProvider(ModelProvider):
    async def generate(model, prompt, ...) -> GenerationResult:
        # POST http://127.0.0.1:13307/api/v1/chat/completions
        # Handle Lemonade recipe/backend system
        
    async def list_models() -> list[str]:
        # GET /api/v1/models
        
    async def health_check() -> dict:
        # GET /api/v1/health + /api/v1/stats
```

### Phase 2: Integrate with CostAwareRouter
- Add Lemonade models to `MODEL_COSTS` dict
- Add Lemonade models to `MODEL_QUALITY` dict (benchmark locally)
- Add Lemonade models to `MODEL_TPS` dict
- CostAwareRouter already selects optimally; just needs executor to use `LemonadeProvider.generate()`

### Phase 3: Lifecycle Management
- Create `LemonadePoolManager` mirroring `ModelPoolManager`
- Call `/api/v1/load`, `/api/v1/unload`, `/api/v1/health`
- Handle recipe/backend state (not just loaded/healthy)

### Phase 4: Cost Integration (if needed)
- Lemonade is local (free), no cost tracking needed
- Can reuse `SessionCostTracker` with $0.00 cost_per_1k

---

## **Files You'll Need to Wire Together**

1. **Create:** `src/cohezion/swarm/providers/lemonade_provider.py` - New provider implementation
2. **Modify:** `src/cohezion/swarm/cost_aware_router.py` - Add Lemonade models to cost/quality/TPS dicts
3. **Create:** `src/cohezion/swarm/lemonade_pool_manager.py` - Lifecycle (optional but recommended)
4. **Integrate:** Wiring point is routing orchestrator or CompoundExecutor that chooses provider at execution time

**No code changes needed to DynamicModelRouter, SmartRouter, or ModelPoolManager themselves—they're provider-agnostic once properly instantiated.**

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**What nobody has ever experienced:** An AI system that you can **watch think** — not as text logs, but as a living multimodal experience. The agent's reasoning becomes a visual landscape (Flux renders the 12D manifold), an evolving soundscape (Kokoro narrates while coherence modulates pitch), and the moment 16 independent bio-cells synchronize through gap junction percolation, you *hear* chaos resolve into harmony and *see* the network crystallize. The cosmogony plays out as 10 visible symmetry breaks — creation itself, rendered locally on your GPU, zero cloud. Nobody has built this because nobody has the physics, the renderer, AND the local inference stack in one system.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Here's the vision in full — what Cohezion + Lemonade creates across all four modalities, with dynamic modularity orchestrating the models:

## The Experience: "Witness an AI Mind"

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    LEMONADE MODEL FABRIC                        │
│                                                                 │
│  NPU (58 TOPS)     │  iGPU (Vulkan)      │  CPU (32 threads)   │
│  ─────────────     │  ──────────────     │  ────────────────   │
│  gemma3-4b-FLM     │  Qwen3-8B-GGUF     │  kokoro-v1 (TTS)   │
│  embed-gemma-300m  │  Flux-2-Klein-4B    │  Whisper-Turbo     │
│  (perception,      │  (reasoning,        │  (narration,       │
│   embeddings)      │   image gen)        │   transcription)   │
│                    │  RealESRGAN (4x)    │                    │
│  ALWAYS LOADED     │  HOTSWAP on demand  │  LOAD when needed  │
└────────┬───────────┴────────┬────────────┴────────┬────────────┘
         │                    │                     │
         ▼                    ▼                     ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              DYNAMIC MODULARITY ROUTER                          │
│                                                                 │
│  CAS Faculty → Model Selection → Slot Management → Inference    │
│                                                                 │
│  Task arrives → classify (NPU, 0ms) → route to device:          │
│    PERCEPTION/ATTENTION  → NPU  (FLM, instant)                  │
│    REASONING/EXECUTIVE   → GPU  (Qwen3, load if needed)         │
│    GENERATION/IMAGE      → GPU  (Flux, hotswap Qwen3 out)       │
│    NARRATION/TTS         → CPU  (kokoro, independent slot)       │
```

```python
    """Orchestrates model loading across NPU/GPU/CPU for multimodal rendering."""

    # Slots: what can run simultaneously
    SLOTS = {
        "npu_llm": "gemma3-4b-FLM",        # always loaded
        "npu_embed": "embed-gemma-300m-FLM", # always loaded
        "gpu": None,                          # hotswap: Qwen3 OR Flux OR RealESRGAN
        "cpu_tts": None,                      # load on demand: kokoro-v1
        "cpu_asr": None,                      # load on demand: Whisper
    }

    def ensure_for_task(self, task_type: str):
        """Load the right model for the current pipeline stage."""
        if task_type == "narrate":
            self._swap_gpu("Qwen3-8B-GGUF")
        elif task_type == "render":
            self._swap_gpu("Flux-2-Klein-4B")
        elif task_type == "upscale":
            self._swap_gpu("RealESRGAN-x4plus")
        elif task_type == "speak":
            self._ensure_cpu("kokoro-v1", slot="cpu_tts")
        elif task_type == "transcribe":
            self._ensure_cpu("Whisper-Large-v3-Turbo", slot="cpu_asr")

        if self.SLOTS["gpu"] != model:
            lemonade_unload_model(self.SLOTS["gpu"])
            lemonade_load_model(model, backend="vulkan")
            self.SLOTS["gpu"] = model
```

content.text:
## Summary: Real-World Lemonade Server Capabilities & Performance Verification

Based on my thorough research of the repository code and web sources, here's what Lemonade can ACTUALLY do on your Radeon 8060S hardware:

---

### 1. **SD-CPP + Vulkan on Linux for AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) - PROBLEMATIC**

**Status:** Works but with significant limitations

- Vulkan is supported on Linux for gfx1151 (RDNA 3.5), using RADV Vulkan driver
- **Critical issue:** Both llama.cpp Vulkan and related inference backends lack certain compute shaders on gfx1151 that fall back to CPU, severely degrading performance
- **Specific Vulkan limitation:** Known GATED_DELTA_NET compute shader missing on RDNA 3.5 (your hardware)
- **Memory allocation problem:** Per-allocation cap (VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::maxMemoryAllocationSize) limited to ~2 GB, causing OOM errors even with 128GB available, especially for large KV caches
- **Performance data:** Vulkan achieves ~850 tok/s for prompt processing on Radeon 8060S with a 7B model—far below ROCm's 1488 tok/s

**Real-world implication:** SD-CPP will work but be CPU-bottlenecked. Not ideal for image generation.

---

### 2. **Kokoro TTS on Linux - YES, WORKS WITH AUDIO**

**Status:** Fully functional, CPU-only

- Kokoro-v1 generates speech 3-11x real-time on CPU
- With modern CPU (Ryzen 5 or better): 3-5x realtime speeds
- Model is lightweight: 82M parameters, 350 MB file size
- **Audio output:** Confirmed working. Linux can play audio via SoX or save to WAV/MP3/OPUS/FLAC
- Your lemonade MCP already supports `lemonade_speak()` which calls `/api/v1/audio/speech` and returns WAV bytes

**Real-world implication:** TTS works great. No GPU needed, CPU is sufficient.

---

### 3. **WhisperCPP with Vulkan on Linux - YES, SUPPORTED**

**Status:** Functional on Linux with Vulkan

- Vulkan backend is integrated and works with AMD/NVIDIA/Intel GPUs
- Available via `GGML_VULKAN=1 pip install` on Linux
- Docker images available pre-compiled with Vulkan
- Works across different GPU vendors on Linux
- **Caveat:** Some Vulkan devices have shared memory limitations for matrix operations, but this is device-specific

**Real-world implication:** Transcription will work on Vulkan. Your MCP supports `lemonade_transcribe()` which calls `/api/v1/audio/transcriptions`.

---

### 4. **Gemma-3-4B-FLM + Pad Token Issue - YES, KNOWN PROBLEM**

**Status:** FLM models are NOT instruction-tuned for chat

- **Root cause:** FLM (FastFlowLM) models are optimization variants focused on efficient NPU/CPU execution on Ryzen AI hardware, NOT chat-tuned
- **Pad token issue:** When you see `<pad>` tokens in output, it's because:
  - FLM models are base/pretrain models optimized for speed, not chat
  - Similar issues reported in Gemma 4: generating infinite `<unused>` tokens on Vulkan backend
  - Thread-safety issues in tool parsing cause pad token degradation when handling multiple requests concurrently
  
- **Alternative:** Use instruction-tuned Gemma models (gemma-3-4b-it, gemma-3-27b-it) or mainstream models like Qwen, Llama instead
- Your MCP line 182-184 already filters out pad tokens: `content = content.replace("<pad>", "").replace("<eos>", "").strip()`

**Real-world implication:** Don't use FLM for chat. Use gemma-3-*-it (instruction-tuned) instead.

---

### 5. **GPU VRAM Situation - UNIFIED MEMORY, NOT DEDICATED VRAM**

**Status:** Complex; shows 0.5GB VRAM but access to 128GB unified memory

**Reality:**
- Radeon 8060S is integrated GPU on Strix Halo (not discrete card)
- Vulkan correctly enumerates total accessible memory (BIOS VRAM + GTT) as ~53-128 GB
- **The 0.5 GB shown is likely the BIOS-reserved framebuffer**
- **GTT (Graphics Translation Table):** Dynamic driver-level extension allowing access to main RAM for GPU computation
- **Actual capability:** Vulkan llama.cpp CAN use the full unified memory pool (not limited to 0.5GB)
- **BUT:** Memory allocation bottleneck — per-allocation cap of ~2GB means you can't load single buffers larger than that, fragmenting memory usage

**Real-world implication:** You have ~128GB accessible but can't allocate buffers > 2GB at a time. This affects large model loading.

---

### 6. **Flux-2-Klein-4B Performance on Radeon 8060S - UNKNOWN, NO BENCHMARKS**

**Status:** No specific benchmarks for 8060S + Flux Klein exist

**What we know:**
- Flux-2-Klein-4B on RTX 4090: **< 0.5 seconds** per 512x512 image (20–60x faster than FLUX.1)
- Fits in ~13GB VRAM on RTX 3090/4070
- 4 inference steps optimized for speed
- **Your hardware:** Radeon 8060S has much lower compute capacity than RTX 4090
- **Estimate (rough):** Likely 2-5x slower than RTX 4090 baseline, so probably **2-5 seconds per image** on Radeon 8060S with Vulkan
- Performance will suffer from the Vulkan memory allocation and missing compute shader issues noted in #1

**Real-world implication:** You can run Flux Klein, but don't expect < 1 second generation. Plan for 2-5 second warmup per image.

---

### 7. **Embeddable Lemonade Server in `vendor/lemonade/` - NOT IN THIS REPO**

**Status:** No vendored Lemonade server found

- Checked `/vendor/` directory: **empty**
- Your project (`lemonade-mcp`) is an **MCP wrapper** around an external Lemonade server running on `http://127.0.0.1:13307`
- It does NOT bundle the Lemonade binary itself
- **Latest available:** Lemonade SDK 10.2 (embeddable binary available separately from GitHub Releases)
- You must **run the separate Lemonade server** and expose it on localhost:13307

**Real-world implication:** MCP is a thin client. Lemonade server must be installed and running separately.

---

### Key Performance Metrics Summary

| Workload | Hardware | Status | Real-world Performance |
|----------|----------|--------|----------------------|
| LLM Chat (7B) | Radeon 8060S Vulkan | Working | ~850 tok/s (prefill) / ~50 tok/s (decode) |
| Image Gen (Flux Klein) | Radeon 8060S Vulkan | Working | ~2-5 sec/512x512 (estimate) |
| TTS (Kokoro) | CPU | Excellent | 3-5x realtime |
| Speech-to-Text (Whisper) | Radeon 8060S Vulkan | Working | Unknown, likely good |
| FLM Models (Gemma-3-4b) | NPU/CPU | Broken for chat | Pad token spam, use -it variants |

---

### Sources

- [AMD Strix Halo GPU Performance](https://llm-tracker.info/AMD-Strix-Halo-(Ryzen-AI-Max+-395)-GPU-Performance)
- [Vulkan gfx1151 missing compute shader issue](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/20354)
- [Vulkan memory allocation cap](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/15054)
- [Kokoro TTS CPU performance](https://ariya.io/2026/03/local-cpu-friendly-high-quality-tts-with-kokoro)
- [Whisper.cpp Vulkan support](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp)
- [Gemma4 infinite token issue](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/21516)
- [Flux-2-Klein performance](https://medium.com/@302.AI/flux-2-klein-test-sub-second-generation-speed-stuns-while-quality-faces-trade-offs-302-ai-c197a73df052)
- [Lemonade SDK 10.2 release](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Lemonade-SDK-10.2-Released)
- [FastFlowLM documentation](https://fastflowlm.com/)
- [Vulkan UMA memory architecture](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/11837)

### 1. **Local Tiny Agents with AMD NPU and iGPU Acceleration** (Most Relevant)
🔗 [huggingface.co/learn/mcp-course/unit2/lemonade-server](https://huggingface.co/learn/mcp-course/unit2/lemonade-server)

This is part of Hugging Face's MCP course. Lemonade Server supports CPU inference across all platforms and engines on Windows x86/x64. GPU acceleration is enabled via the llamacpp engine using Vulkan, with a focus on AMD Ryzen™ AI 7000/8000/300 series and AMD Radeon™ 7000/9000 series.

For Windows applications that require a concise context and would benefit from NPU + iGPU acceleration, you can try the Hybrid models available with Lemonade Server — optimized for AMD Ryzen AI 300 series PCs. Models such as Llama-xLAM-2-8b-fc-r-Hybrid are specifically fine-tuned for tool-calling and deliver fast, responsive performance.

In this unit, they show how to accelerate an end-to-end Tiny Agents application with AMD NPU and iGPU, and how to create an assistant to handle sensitive information locally.

---

### 2. **Models Running on Lemonade**
🔗 [huggingface.co/models?apps=lemonade&sort=trending](https://huggingface.co/models?apps=lemonade&sort=trending)

Hugging Face has a dedicated filter for models running on Lemonade, listing models across categories including Image-Text-to-Text and Text Generation, with various model sizes available.

---

### 3. **LEMONADE Dataset (amathislab)**
🔗 [huggingface.co/datasets/amathislab/LEMONADE](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amathislab/LEMONADE)

This is a different "Lemonade" — a benchmark dataset. It introduces LEMONADE: Language models Evaluation of MOtion aNd Action-Driven Enquiries. Lemonade consists of 36,521 closed-ended QA pairs linked to egocentric video clips, categorized in three groups and six subcategories.

---

### 4. **AMD GPU for Local Inference (Forum Discussion)**
🔗 [discuss.huggingface.co/t/amd-gpu-for-local-inference/167932](https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/amd-gpu-for-local-inference/167932)

A community forum thread where a user discusses buying an AMD GPU for local AI experiments using the transformers and diffusers libraries with Hugging Face models, noting their current AMD RX 5600XT is not supported by ROCm, and considering AMD cards for Linux compatibility.

---

### 5. **Hugging Face Pipelines Documentation**
🔗 [huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main_classes/pipelines](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main_classes/pipelines)

The pipelines are a great and easy way to use models for inference, offering a simple API dedicated to several tasks, including Named Entity Recognition, Masked Language Modeling, Sentiment Analysis, Feature Extraction and Question Answering. Task-specific pipelines are available for audio, computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal tasks.

---

The **most relevant result** is the first one — the Hugging Face MCP course unit on **Lemonade Server**, which covers local inference with AMD hardware acceleration (NPU/iGPU/GPU) combined with Tiny Agents for agentic workflows.

Here are the search results for your query on GitHub related to "lemonade-sdk MCP server tools integration":

---

## Key Results

### 1. **lemonade-sdk/lemonade** (Main Repository)
**URL:** https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade

Lemonade is the local AI server that gives you the same capabilities as cloud APIs, except 100% free and private. It supports the latest models for chat, coding, speech, and image generation on your own NPU and GPU.

- You can use any OpenAI-compatible client library by configuring it to use `http://localhost:13305/v1` as the base URL.
- Lemonade supports the Ollama API, allowing applications built for Ollama to work with Lemonade without modification.
- Lemonade supports an initial Anthropic Messages compatibility endpoint for applications that call Claude-style APIs.

### 2. **Server Integration Guide** (`lemonade-sdk/lemonade`)
**URL:** https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/blob/main/docs/server/server_integration.md

This guide provides instructions on how to integrate Lemonade Server into your application. There are two main ways in which Lemonade Server might integrate into apps: User-Managed Server (user installs/manages) or App-Managed Server (app installs/manages on behalf of the user).

### 3. **amd/gaia Releases** (MCP Integration with Lemonade)
**URL:** https://github.com/amd/gaia/releases

MCP responses now capture inference statistics from SSE events, giving you visibility into model performance during tool-augmented conversations.

New features include a C++17 Agent Framework with full native agent framework with MCP support, tool registry, and state machine — no Python needed.

One release focuses on streamlined setup experience with improvements to `gaia init`, Lemonade 9.1.4 compatibility, and an expanded MCP ecosystem roadmap.

### 4. **Lemonade Stand MCP Server** (Fun Example Project)
**URL:** https://github.com/jimmcq/Lemonade-Stand-MCP-Server

A simple, working example of a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets you play the classic Lemonade Stand game through Claude Desktop. This server demonstrates how MCP works by implementing the classic Lemonade Stand game as a set of tools that Claude can use.

*(Note: This is a different project — a game, not part of the lemonade-sdk.)*

### 5. **lemonade-sdk Organization Overview**
**URL:** https://github.com/lemonade-sdk

Lemonade Server is the flagship repo that ties everything together. llamacpp-rocm is their build system for llama.cpp ROCm that uses TheRock. marketplace is where you can submit apps for inclusion on the Lemonade app and website. lemonade-eval is a benchmarking and accuracy evaluation client for Lemonade Server.

### 6. **Lemonade Releases** (Latest Versions)
**URL:** https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/releases

- Embeddable Lemonade is now available! Package Lemonade's capabilities into your own app with this portable binary. No Lemonade installer or branding needed.
- The `lemonade-server` CLI is deprecated and will be removed in the next release after May 6, 2026.

---

**Summary:** The `lemonade-sdk` organization on GitHub focuses on a local AI server platform (not an MCP server itself), while the **amd/gaia** project provides the most relevant MCP + tools integration that connects with Lemonade Server. The "Lemonade Stand MCP Server" is a separate, unrelated fun project demonstrating MCP with a classic game.

Here are the results from the search on arxiv.org for papers related to **agent reasoning, visualization, diffusion, sonification, and multimodal** topics from 2025–2026. While the search returned several relevant papers on multimodal agents, reasoning, visualization, and diffusion, **no single paper was found that specifically combines all of these topics together with sonification**. Here's a summary of the most relevant papers found:

---

### 1. **Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation Models** (arXiv: 2505.02567)
Models discussed include any-to-any multimodal models, capable of handling inputs or outputs beyond text and image, such as audio, video, and speech. The paper explores combining the strengths of autoregressive models for reasoning and text generation with the robustness of diffusion-based models for high-quality image synthesis.

### 2. **Agent-X: Evaluating Deep Multimodal Reasoning in Vision-Centric Agentic Tasks** (arXiv: 2505.24876)
Agent-X features 828 agentic tasks with authentic visual contexts, including images, multi-image comparisons, videos, and instructional text. These tasks span six major agentic environments: general visual reasoning, web browsing, security and surveillance, autonomous driving, sports, and math.

### 3. **Agentic Artificial Intelligence: Architectures, Taxonomies** (arXiv: 2601.12560, Jan 2026)
The agent brain transforms each observation into a reasoning trace using hierarchical planning and self-reflection. Perception has moved from processing only raw text to handling visual, multimodal, and audio inputs, which allows agents to use persistent storage backed by vector databases and RAG.

### 4. **Agent-Omni: Test-Time Multimodal Reasoning via Model Coordination** (arXiv: 2511.02834, Nov 2025)
The Agent-Omni framework coordinates existing foundation models through a master-agent system, where the master agent interprets user intent, delegates subtasks to modality-specific agents, and integrates their outputs into coherent responses. Extensive experiments across text, image, audio, video, and omni benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance, particularly on tasks requiring complex cross-modal reasoning.

### 5. **MARS2 2025 Challenge on Multimodal Reasoning** (arXiv: 2509.14142, Sep 2025)
This challenge aims to bring together different approaches in multimodal machine learning and LLMs, focusing on real-world and specialized scenarios to broaden the multimodal reasoning applications of MLLMs. Their approach includes global understanding via audio-visual integration, where audio in video is transcribed by automatic speech recognition tools.

### 6. **M3-Agent: Seeing, Listening, Remembering, and Reasoning** (arXiv: 2508.09736, Aug 2025)
M3-Agent is a novel multimodal agent framework equipped with long-term memory that can process real-time visual and auditory inputs to build and update episodic and semantic memories. Given an instruction, M3-Agent autonomously performs multi-turn reasoning and retrieves relevant memories to complete tasks.

### 7. **MultiVis-Agent: Cross-Modal Data Visualization** (arXiv: 2601.18320, Jan 2026)
In visualization, early agent-based frameworks focused on specialized agents for data understanding, visual mapping, and layout optimization. They developed MultiVis-Bench, a benchmark with over 1,000 cases for multi-modal visualization evaluation, achieving 75.63% visualization score on challenging tasks.

### 8. **AgentVista: Evaluating Multimodal Agents in Ultra-Challenging Realistic Visual Scenarios** (arXiv: 2602.23166, Mar 2026)
AgentVista is a benchmark for evaluating generalist multimodal agents on realistic, ultra-challenging tasks that require long-horizon, interleaved tool use grounded in visual evidence. Even the best model in their evaluation, Gemini-3-Pro with tools, achieves only 27.3% overall accuracy.

---

**Note:** The specific combination of **sonification** with agent reasoning, visualization, and diffusion in a multimodal context did not appear in these results. ## AMD GAIA — AI Agent Framework on GitHub

GAIA is AMD's open-source framework for building intelligent AI agents that run 100% locally on AMD Ryzen AI hardware. It keeps your data private, eliminates cloud costs, and deploys in air-gapped environments—all with hardware-accelerated performance.

### Key Results

1. **[github.com/amd/gaia](https://github.com/amd/gaia)** (Main Repo)
   - A C++17 port of the GAIA base agent framework is available under `cpp/`. It implements the same agent loop, tool registry, and MCP client interface without any Python dependency — suitable for embedding in native applications or resource-constrained environments.
   - GAIA uses Lemonade Server to provide optimal performance on Ryzen AI hardware.

2. **[Releases (amd/gaia)](https://github.com/amd/gaia/releases)**
   - Major release introducing the C++17 Agent Framework — a native port of the GAIA agent system that lets you build AI PC agents in pure C++ with no Python runtime required. Also includes security hardening across the Python codebase and a comprehensive documentation site reorganization. The new C++17 Agent Framework features full native agent framework with MCP support, tool registry, and state machine.
   - MCP responses now capture inference statistics from SSE events, giving visibility into model performance during tool-augmented conversations.

3. **[Docker Guide (docs/guides/docker.mdx)](https://github.com/amd/gaia/blob/main/docs/guides/docker.mdx)**
   - GAIA's MCP support is powered by FastMCP from the Model Context Protocol Python SDK.
   - The server supports JSON-RPC interface and works with GitHub Copilot, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients.
   - Copyright is listed as "Copyright(C) 2024-2026 Advanced Micro Devices, Inc."

4. **[CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/amd/gaia/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)** — Contains the project's agent and specialist structure:
   - Includes specialized agents such as `gaia-agent-builder` for creating new GAIA agents, tool registration, and state management; `mcp-developer` for MCP server implementation and WebSocket protocols; and many others.
   - The source tree includes agents for chat (with RAG), code orchestration, Blender 3D automation, Jira issue management, Docker containerization, medical intake (EMR), routing, and Stable Diffusion image generation.

5. **[CLI Documentation (docs/cli.md)](https://github.com/amd/gaia/blob/main/docs/cli.md)**
   - The MCP (Model Context Protocol) command provides integration with MCP-compatible clients and external services like Atlassian's Jira, Confluence, and Compass. MCP enables GAIA to connect with Claude Desktop, VS Code, Cursor, and custom applications through a standardized WebSocket-based protocol.

6. **[v0.17.0 Release](https://github.com/amd/gaia/releases/tag/v0.17.0)**
   - GAIA v0.17.0 lets you run AI agents locally on your PC — analyze documents, execute tools, and accomplish tasks without sending data to the cloud. It introduces the Agent UI.
   - This release adds a safety layer with a confirmation popup (Allow, Deny, or Always Allow) before `run_shell_command` and other write/execute tools, with a 60-second auto-deny timeout.

All results are scoped to `github.com/amd/gaia`, covering MCP agent capabilities, Lemonade Server integration, and tool support through the 2024–2026 timeframe.

### 1. **[lemonade-sdk/lemonade](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade)** (Main Repository)
This project is built by the community for every PC, with optimizations by AMD engineers to get the most from Ryzen AI, Radeon, and Strix Halo PCs. Lemonade supports a wide variety of LLMs (GGUF, FLM, and ONNX), whisper, stable diffusion, etc. across CPU, GPU, and NPU.

Lemonade Server supports CPU inference across all platforms and engines on Windows x86/x64. For GPU acceleration is enabled through llamacpp engine (Vulkan), with a focus on AMD Ryzen™ AI 7000/8000/300 series and Radeon™ 7000/9000 series. Models such as Llama-xLAM-2-8b-fc-r-Hybrid are specifically fine-tuned for tool-calling and deliver fast, responsive performance!

### 3. **[amd/gaia – Releases](https://github.com/amd/gaia/releases)**
MCP responses now capture inference statistics from SSE events, giving you visibility into model performance during tool-augmented conversations. New: C++17 Agent Framework — Full native agent framework with MCP support, tool registry, and state machine — no Python needed. GAIA now detects when your running Lemonade Server version differs from the expected version and displays a clear warning with upgrade instructions.

### 4. **[lemonade-sdk/llamacpp-rocm](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/llamacpp-rocm)**
We provide nightly builds of llama.cpp with AMD ROCm™ 7 acceleration based on TheRock. Our automated pipeline specifically targets seamless integration with 🍋 Lemonade and similar AI applications requiring high-performance GPU inference.

### 5. **[BerriAI/litellm – PR #14840: Add AMD Lemonade Provider](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/14840)**
This PR adds support for a litellm provider backed by Lemonade Server, a high-performance local LLM inference server optimized for GPUs and NPUs. Lemonade Server provides an OpenAI-compatible API that enables developers to run LLMs locally with...

### 6. **[lemonade-sdk/llamacpp-rocm-dll](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/llamacpp-rocm-dll)**
This build specifically targets GPU architectures including gfx110X (RDNA3 GPUs) — AMD Radeon PRO W7900/W7800/W7700/V710, RX 7900 XTX/XT/GRE, RX 7800 XT, RX 7700 XT. 🍋 Lemonade Integration: You can also test these builds directly with Lemonade for a seamless AI application experience (coming soon!)

### 7. **[amd/gaia – CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/amd/gaia/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)**
This file details the GAIA project structure, which uses Lemonade Server as its LLM backend. It defines specialized roles like "lemonade-specialist (opus) - Lemonade Server, AMD NPU/GPU optimization" and includes skills for MCP session inspection, eval benchmarking, and RAG cache integrity.

### 8. **[lemonade-sdk/lemonade – Server Spec](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/blob/main/docs/server/server_spec.md)**
Lemonade helps users discover and run local AI apps by serving optimized LLMs right from their own GPUs and NPUs. The server spec covers endpoints for model management, chat completions, and configuration — noting that this server is intended for use on local systems only. Do not expose the server port to the open internet.

Here's a summary of what I found regarding **stable-diffusion.cpp (sd-cpp)** and **Stable Diffusion image generation** on the **AMD Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo** with **Vulkan**:

---

## Direct sd-cpp + Vulkan on Strix Halo / Radeon 8060S

### stable-diffusion.cpp Bug Report (Feb 2026)

A user running stable-diffusion.cpp on a Strix Halo system (AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S) reported that generating 1 latent image completed in **489.92 seconds** (for FLUX dev Q8_0 at 1024×1024, 50 steps), but the process then failed during VAE decoding with a Vulkan out-of-memory error.

This was on a Strix Halo setup with 96GB available for Vulkan (out of total 128GB), and there was more than enough memory — the inference ran fine for 50 steps and only failed at the end. nvtop showed low memory utilization.

The HIP version works with the same parameters, but HIP/ROCm for Strix Halo is "very unstable," so Vulkan is more preferable. The user notes that llama.cpp with Vulkan works without issues, with performance very close to HIP.

### Z-Image-Turbo with sd-cpp + Vulkan (Dec 2025)

One user, as of December 2025, spent a long time trying to get ComfyUI and Automatic1111 working on a Framework Desktop (Ryzen AI Max+ 395) with Fedora, but ROCm "just isn't ready for Strix Halo yet — constant GPU hangs, memory errors." The recommended approach: "Skip ROCm, use stable-diffusion.cpp with Vulkan."

stable-diffusion.cpp was described as "the missing link." Vulkan bypasses ROCm entirely using Mesa's RADV driver, which has excellent RDNA 3.5 support and is friendlier to the unified memory architecture.

---

## Other Stable Diffusion Benchmarks on Strix Halo

### Framework Community (Aug 2025)

A Framework Community member noted that someone running a Stable Diffusion clone posted details of an image generation benchmark on Strix Halo, and described the result as "underwhelming." They pointed users to the SD WebUI Benchmark Data to search for "8060S."

### AMD Amuse AI / NPU Performance (Phoronix Forums)

AMD published "Amuse AI" which supports NPU-accelerated image generation with 2 models (SDXL and Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium). Testing showed atrocious performance — even with the NPU's supposed 50 TOPS, Amuse AI only manages 0.33 iterations/second with SD3.5 Medium at 1024×1024 on the top-end Strix Halo chip.

The poster was "certain running the same on the integrated GPU using Vulkan would be faster, even though the GPU is theoretically slower than the NPU." The Strix Halo GPU has a theoretical maximum of 59.4 FP16 TFLOPS.

### DGX Spark Comparison (Starry Hope, Feb 2026)

The NVIDIA DGX Spark "dominates in image generation workloads, pushing about 2.5x the performance of Strix Halo with FLUX models."

---

## Key Takeaways

1. **No formal sd-cpp benchmark suite results** were found specifically for the Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo with Vulkan. The community is still working through stability and memory issues.

2. The one concrete sd-cpp data point shows **~490 seconds for a FLUX dev Q8_0 image** (1024×1024, 50 steps) on Vulkan, though this run failed at VAE decode due to a Vulkan buffer size limit bug.
